newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent in range, bear flag may be forming.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent in range, bear flag may be forming.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+Brent remains in a range and some may argue that a base is in place which could serve as a springboard for another attack on the upside gap at $18.64-$18.77.

+But the consolidative action from the beginning of the month has created a pattern which looks to some like a bear flag - and with momentum indicators nearing overbought territory, this could spell another downwards move out of the range.

IPE Brent crude oil futures were thought likely to trade sideways again on Tuesday but technical analysts differed as to whether recent consolidative business could serve as a base from which to attack the upside gap between $18.64 and $18.77.
June Brent closed just a cent down on Monday at $18.26 a barrel, while May gas oil was just 25 cents a tonne firmer at $165.75.
"We have nicely defined patterns and ranges on the technicals and await fresh signals," MeesPierson Derivatives in London said of world energy markets in their daily report.
They located a range for June Brent, using their Market Profile chart technique, between $17.92 and $18.36.
Steve Kwan at MMS in London also said the market was "consolidative."

"There are two interpretations: either the recent action has been base-forming, in which case we are set to test the gap to $18.77, or this is a bear flag pattern which means we are going to break lower."
"And looking at the momentum patterns, the bias is down. We need to close higher through the gap to get bullish again."
May Gas oil is still facing resistance at $167 a tonne, the highest point reached this month, and the market has also failed to break below $165 in the past few days.
"We are into good support now at $165," MeesPierson said. "Perhaps buy a little here, looking to sell at $166.75."
